D1: BER INTEGER minimal sign representation

X.690 §8.3.2, source: secondary. The subject's `ASN1Integer.swift` comment quotes the rule: “a) shall not all be ones; and b) shall not all be zero.” It also explains that the rule ensures the smallest possible number of octets. This is a BER rule, so it also applies before the DER restrictions.

Minimal input: `\x02\x02\x00\x00`; hex `02 02 00 00`. Expected: a thrown encoding error. Actual: `Int(berEncoded:)` returns zero. `02 02 ff ff` similarly returns minus one. The DER initializer rejects these redundant encodings. The BER initializer omits the minimality check.

Reproduction: `python3 acceptance/deviation_one.py 1`. The specification assertion in `deviation_1_ber_integer_minimal` fails against the published dependency. The same assertion fails against main. The supplied issue and PR lists contain signed INTEGER fixes (#124 and issue #52), but neither describes redundant BER sign octets. #124's diff was read; issue #52's title was read. The supplied known/*.json snapshots hold titles. Confidence: high for the reproduced behaviour; the clause is a secondary citation because the X.690 PDF was unavailable.

D2: PEM newline conventions

RFC 7468 §2: “MUST handle different newline conventions.” Section 3 includes CRLF, CR and LF in `eol`. These are primary citations from the supplied RFC text.

Minimal nonempty document used by the test: `-----BEGIN A-----\rAA==\r-----END A-----`; hex `2d2d2d2d2d424547494e20412d2d2d2d2d0d41413d3d0d2d2d2d2d2d454e4420412d2d2d2d2d`. Expected: one zero byte. Actual: `invalidPEMDocument`. The corresponding LF and CRLF documents pass.

Reproduction: `python3 acceptance/deviation_one.py 2`. `deviation_2_pem_cr_line_endings` fails against the published dependency and main. Issue #66 describes Windows CRLF, so it is adjacent historical evidence rather than a matching CR-only issue. Confidence: high. Handling CR is mandatory; optional whitespace leniency is a separate item.

D4: encoder bug producing malformed GeneralizedTime from the public Double initializer

X.690 §11.7, source: secondary. The subject's `TimeUtilities.swift` comment states that there “may be fractional seconds but they must not have trailing zeros.” Its component initializer documents a numerical fractional-seconds parameter without a minimum positive value. The implementation checks `0 <= fractionalSeconds < 1` before formatting it.

Minimal API reproduction: a valid calendar value with `fractionalSeconds: 0.00001`. Expected: a value that serializes as `20260101000000.00001Z`, or a thrown error where the value cannot be represented. Actual in debug: process termination at `TimeUtilities.swift:218`, at the assertion that `String(fractionalSeconds)` starts with `0.`. Swift formats this Double in exponent notation. The equivalent DER bytes `18 15 32 30 32 36 30 31 30 31 30 30 30 30 30 30 2e 30 30 30 30 31 5a` parse successfully; the content is `20260101000000.00001Z`. The smaller values `0.000001` and `1e-20` also abort, while `0.1` succeeds. This is a programmatic-input failure, not an observed byte-parser crash.

Reproduction: `python3 acceptance/deviation_one.py 4`. `deviation_4_small_fractional_seconds` fails by process termination in debug on both versions. In independently built `-c release` harnesses it fails its exact-byte assertion and round trip: the constructor serializes `20260101000000.-05Z` (DER hex `18 13 32 30 32 36 30 31 30 31 30 30 30 30 30 30 2e 2d 30 35 5a`). The `-05` fractional field breaks the GeneralizedTime syntax and cannot be parsed back; this is an encoder bug, beyond the DER trailing-zero rule. Release asserts are removed. `String(Double)` returns `1e-05`, and dropping the first two characters produces `-05`. `evidence/gen/d4-build-modes.json` records both modes and both subjects; the isolated test and probe logs provide execution evidence. A value parsed from `20260101000000.00001Z` preserves raw digits and reserializes exactly in both modes; `testParsedSmallFractionRoundTrip` passes. The captured programmatic reproduction covers the public Double constructor. The public `fractionalSeconds` setter calls the same conversion helper (`GeneralizedTime.swift:109`); setter exposure is source-derived and has not been separately captured. The supplied issue and PR lists have no matching item, and the affected implementation is unchanged on main. Confidence: high for the reproduced debug abort, release bytes, parsed round trip and pinned version comparison. The exact normative range remains a secondary-source limitation; the stronger directly reproduced fact is that the documented throwing constructor aborts for a value inside its own checked range.

K1: EOC handling

X.690 §8.1.3.6.1, source: secondary. The subject comment says the clause “requires end-of-contents octets.” Local main's #134 diff says that the octets terminate contents at the current level.

Minimal tag-zero input: `\x00\x00`, hex `00 00`. Expected: rejection as a standalone value. Actual: accepted by DER and BER. A nesting example is `30 80 30 02 00 00`: the terminator inside a definite child incorrectly satisfies the outer indefinite container. Local main rejects both. `testKnownUniversalZero` is red on 1.7.3 and green on main. Classification: KNOWN, fixed but unreleased. Confidence: high for the version comparison; normative citation remains secondary.

K2: OID first pair

X.690 §8.19, source: secondary. The subject quotes the first-subidentifier formula as “(X*40) + Y” and states that the first arc has only the values 0, 1 and 2, with the second arc limited to 39 only for arcs 0 and 1.

Input: `06 01 78`, escaped `\x06\x01\x78`. Expected components: `[2, 40]`. Actual: `[3, 0]`. `testKnownOIDSecondArc` fails on both versions. Open PR #132 matches this behaviour. Confidence: high. The distinct, valid `[1,39]` boundary is a mutation-backed package discriminator. It is deferred from the PR patch because open #132 already adds `(79, [1, 39])`, as checked by the supplied cold review. Mutant 21 fires only on input byte 79; this differs from the existing decoding bug above.

K3: invalid UTF-8

X.690 §8.23, source: secondary. The public doc comment describes UTF8String as “a string made up of UTF-8 bytes.” Input `0c 01 ff` (`\x0c\x01\xff`) is accepted and retained, although `ff` cannot be a UTF-8 encoding. `testKnownUTF8Validation` is red on both versions. Open PR #129 matches the finding. Confidence: high for the byte behaviour; broader character-set authority is limited to secondary sources.

K4: BMPString and UniversalString content validation

X.690 §8.23, source: secondary. The public comments describe these types as opaque sequences of bytes. Inputs `1e 01 00` and `1c 01 00` are retained rather than rejected for incomplete code units. Issue #130 names missing content validation and matches these decoding observations. The relevant source is unchanged on pinned main. Confidence: high for the reproduced bytes; broader character-set authority remains secondary. Teletex interpretation remains an unclaimed semantic gap.

D5: UniversalString literal conversion

X.690 §8.23, source: secondary. UniversalString requires four-octet character encoding. Minimal input: `ASN1UniversalString(stringLiteral: "A")`; Unicode scalar U+0041. Expected bytes: `00 00 00 41`. Actual bytes: UTF-8 `41`. The public string-literal initializer converts a String, rather than accepting caller-supplied raw bytes; the opaque storage description does not document this conversion deviation. Issue #130 only names content validation, and no supplied issue or PR names this initializer by content. This item is therefore classified independently as DEVIATION. The same bytes are reproduced on pinned main. `test_deviation_5_universal_string_literal` fails on both versions; `python3 acceptance/deviation_one.py 5` reproduces it. Confidence: high for the conversion; normative authority is secondary. Issue [#110](https://github.com/apple/swift-asn1/issues/110) and merged fix [#111](https://github.com/apple/swift-asn1/pull/111) provide precedent: BMPString's literal initializer also stored UTF-8 bytes until #111 changed it to UTF-16 code units in big-endian order. The local #111 diff was read. That fix does not cover this UniversalString initializer.

L1: PEM parser leniency

RFC 7468 §2 says parsers “SHOULD ignore whitespace” and “MAY handle other line sizes.” The module's comments prescribe exactly 64 characters on nonfinal lines and a nonempty final line of at most 64. A body ` A A== ` is rejected. This optional/recommended leniency is not treated as a new MUST violation. LF and CRLF handling both pass. A decoder may accept nonzero base64 pad bits under RFC 4648 §3.5; accepting `AB==` is therefore not a deviation. Main retains the same parser policy.

L2: BER support limits

X.690 §8.6 and timestamp rules, source: secondary. The BIT STRING implementation says “Constructed encoding of ASN1BitString not yet supported.” The shipped `testConstructedBitString` expects an error for `23 08 03 02 00 ab 03 02 04 0c`. `GeneralizedTime` contains an explicit TODO for relaxed BER timestamp parsing; its BER initializer uses the strict DER grammar. These are documented restrictions. The serializer's raw-byte entry point also explicitly requires well-formed DER from the caller; arbitrary raw-byte output is not claimed to be canonical. Main retains these restrictions.

A1: final newline

RFC 7468 §3 standard grammar has `[eol]` after the closing boundary; its strict grammar requires `eol`. New generators SHOULD emit the strict form. A nonempty PEMDocument emits LF-separated lines and no terminal LF. The grammar accepts this, but the recommendation points to a different form. Confidence: high for the output; no mandatory deviation is claimed. Main emits the same form.

## Notes

D3: PEM caller-label handling (API-hardening note)

RFC 7468 §2 excludes spaces or hyphens at either end of a label; §3 defines the label grammar. The caller supplies the label as a String, and the generator copies it verbatim. The parser round-trips the generator's output, including the one-space label. Label validation or a documented valid-label precondition would harden this API. This observation is not classified as a conformance deviation and is excluded from the issue list.

Input: discriminator `" "` and valid DER NULL bytes `05 00`; discriminator hex `20`. Actual: `-----BEGIN  -----\nBQA=\n-----END  -----`. The one-space label lies outside the RFC grammar, but parsing that generated document returns the original DER NULL bytes on both tag and pinned main. The reference corpus also checks trailing spaces, repeated spaces, repeated hyphens and embedded newlines. `evidence/gen/pem-label-valid-der.json` retains the original generation observation.

Reproduction: `python3 acceptance/deviation_one.py 3`. The retained test `deviation_3_pem_generator_label` asserts the whole label grammar and fails on both versions. Its historical name and expected-red output are kept for evidence continuity; they do not establish a deviation classification. Classification: API-hardening note. Confidence: high for the observed generation and round trip.

In `testRejectDripFedASN1SPKIP256` (ASN1Tests.swift:241), `index == endIndex` is never true inside `indices`, so the success branch is not exercised. The test checks truncated prefixes; a full-input case would also exercise successful parsing. This is a coverage note, not a claim that the existing rejection checks are broken.

## Checked with no deviation in the declared cases

The deterministic corpus uses seed `6902021`. The initial corpus contained 153,146 requests; the revised corpus contains 153,206 requests: every zero-, one- and two-byte envelope under both DER and BER; generated OCTET STRING envelopes; truncation at every position of each generated envelope; one-byte edits; four tag classes and high-tag boundaries; BOOLEAN values; INTEGER sign boundaries; BIT STRING unused counts and 54 nonempty payload/padding cases; six real SET OF cases; string alphabet byte classes; OID subidentifiers; time character edits and truncations; PEM payload sizes 1 through 160; and newline and label variants, plus four programmatic fractional-second inputs. The complete count by operation is recorded with classification evidence.

No additional differences were observed for minimal DER INTEGER values, DER BOOLEAN canonicality, BIT STRING zero padding, PrintableString/VisibleString/IA5String byte alphabets, the tested valid time syntax, or PEM wrapping and base64 generation. No byte-input crash or timeout was observed in either reference run. Three programmatic fractional-second inputs abort on each version, as recorded in D4. The shipped and proposed tests supply typed serializer round trips. The independent reference now directly checks real SET OF ordering and nonempty BIT STRING padding. The SET dispatch uses tag number 17; 0x31 is its constructed wire identifier. The reference also compares reserialized DER framing against the original valid envelope. This is bounded evidence, not a guarantee for arbitrary-length input.

The API has no incremental input interface. The truncation corpus checks prefixes; it does not claim streaming equivalence. Valid inputs deeper than the implementation's limit of 50 are outside the error-contract corpus. CER, certificate-specific time selection, arbitrary custom protocol conformances, concurrency laws, all synthesized collection operations, and unbounded resource use are explicit gaps or declared inapplicable. The unavailable X.690 PDF limits all X.690 rows to `source = "secondary"`; the README states the same limit.
